run.question: What is the distribution of events by service in the 'app-183d-events' index? Give me the count of events for each service.

report.summary: In the authorized window (2026-11-20T04:34:07Z to 2026-11-21T04:34:07Z) the Elasticsearch index app-183d-events returned 10 documents (total, relation eq) distributed across three service values: payment-api 5, order-service 3 and inventory-api 2 (with sum_other_doc_count 0, so these three buckets account for all 10 matching documents). The index itself holds 10 documents in total and is green/open, and all 10 documents matched inside the window; their own timestamp values run from 2026-11-21T02:31:00Z to 2026-11-21T04:32:00Z, so there are no documents with an earlier timestamp in this index at query time. Every one of those 10 documents carries event_type "request", so the per-service distribution describes request events only. The distribution is window-dependent: restricted to the default 1-hour window ending at the authorized window end (2026-11-21T03:34:07Z to 04:34:07Z), only 2 documents matched, both inventory-api. This is a counting question, not a fault investigation; no service health, error or latency conclusion is drawn and no root cause is named.

claims.text: The index app-183d-events exists in the otel-demo Elasticsearch source with health green, status open and docs.count 10 (store.size 7.9kb); this is the index state at query time and no other index name matched the pattern app-183d-events*.

The app-183d-events mapping defines four fields: service (keyword), event_type (keyword), timestamp (date) and duration_ms (integer); there is no @timestamp field, so timestamp must be supplied as time_field for time filtering.

A terms aggregation on the service field over the full authorized window (2026-11-20T04:34:07Z to 2026-11-21T04:34:07Z) returned total 10 documents (relation eq) with buckets payment-api 5, order-service 3 and inventory-api 2, each with doc_count_error_upper_bound 0 and sum_other_doc_count 0.

The 10 documents matched in the authorized window are, by service and timestamp: payment-api at 02:31:00Z, 02:32:00Z, 02:33:00Z, 02:34:00Z and 02:35:00Z; order-service at 03:31:00Z, 03:32:00Z and 03:33:00Z; inventory-api at 04:31:00Z and 04:32:00Z; all on 2026-11-21 and all with event_type "request" (duration_ms 110-320).

The distribution depends on the window used: with the tool's default 1-hour window 2026-11-21T03:34:07Z to 04:34:07Z, the same aggregation matched only 2 documents, all inventory-api (event_type "request"), so a one-hour view omits the payment-api and order-service documents.

Counting the same index over the whole authorized window is limited in time coverage: the returned documents' source_start_at/source_end_at span only 2026-11-21T02:31:00Z to 04:32:00Z, i.e. roughly the last two hours of the 24-hour window contain all index content (consistent with the index holding 10 documents in total), so this index cannot show events from most of the authorized window.

gaps: One documents query that combined a source field filter with an explicit ascending sort on timestamp was rejected as INVALID_PARAMS with no documents returned; the same document listing without those parameters succeeded, so the rejected request contributes no evidence.

The event_type dimension was only observed for the 10 returned documents (all "request"); no per-service event_type aggregation was obtained for the full window, so whether other event_type values exist per service in the index is not established.

Retention and ingest delay for app-183d-events are unknown, so the absence of documents with timestamps before 2026-11-21T02:31:00Z inside the authorized window may reflect retention rather than no events occurring.

The service names in this index (payment-api, order-service, inventory-api) were not cross-checked against any other telemetry source, so how they map to the traces/metrics service identities is unknown.
next_steps: If a per-event_type breakdown per service is needed, run a terms aggregation on event_type nested under the service aggregation over the full authorized window.

If these events are to be correlated with a fault, verify how the index's service values (payment-api, order-service, inventory-api) map to the trace/metric service identifiers before attributing any error or latency signal to them.
